issue_description: Ship Date - Order Date is 904-1642 days for every row and ship mode explains only 0.1% of its variance. This raw gap is NOT a delivery lead time and is never used as one.

The Order ID year (2021-2024) is the original order year: Order Date years were relabelled (two original years per new year) and Ship Date is the original ship date shifted by a constant 2000 days. Dates in this file are therefore synthetic/disguised and calendar values (year, weekday) of Order Date and Ship Date must not be interpreted literally.

lead_time_recovered_days = Ship Date - shift - (Order Date with Order ID year). It is a DERIVED value under a testable rule (ship mode explains 67% of its variance; Same Day rows are ~0 days), not a measured delivery duration. 10194 rows recovered; 0 set to missing.

7 products have fewer than 30 order lines: Laffy Taffy (10), SweeTARTS (10), Fizzy Lifting Drinks (6), Nerds (4), Hair Toffee (4), Everlasting Gobstopper (3), Fun Dip (3). Estimates for these products rest on very little data.

Canadian rows use approximate province geographic centres; for large provinces these can be hundreds of miles from customers' cities, so their distances are less reliable than US state-centroid distances.
28 customers ship to more than one state/province. Geography is taken from each order line, not from the customer record.
Rows identical in every column except Row ID. They may be genuine repeat lines or duplicates; the source gives no way to tell, so they are kept and flagged, not removed.

Order ID embeds Customer ID and Product ID, so it identifies an order line group, not a basket: 8549 distinct Order IDs for 10194 lines (3018 lines share an ID). 'Orders' counts in this system mean distinct Order IDs.
US postal codes with 4 digits (leading zero lost, e.g. New England). Postal codes are not used for distance, so this does not affect calculations.
0 missing or blank cells across 18 columns.
Gross Profit = Sales - Cost holds for 10194 of 10194 rows.

The source has no factory-specific production cost, freight rate, factory capacity or product-factory compatibility data. Unit cost is constant per product. All such inputs are configurable analyst assumptions.
